answer: A live individuality ceremony holds back the tide of bulk fake identities. Applicants meet in groves of twenty seats, each bound to one fingerprint and a 60-credit bond. They answer fresh prompts in ten minutes, so one operator cannot fill two seats. A cluster matching too closely falls to the nadir, loses its bonds, and is frozen one epoch. Hired stand-ins fail: one stand-in fills one seat, so the kth fake still needs a new person and 60 credits. 1,000 fakes cost 60,000 credits, rising linearly, while an honest agent pays 60 once and recovers it after a clean ceremony.
